summary.intent: Plan and then execute GSD roadmap phase 68.2 (SDK-owned read chain and resolved folder listings) end-to-end — research, scope decisions, planning, verification — and then drive wave-based execution, while also spinning up an isolated worktree to parallelize phase 69 planning.
summary.outcome: Phase 68.2 was fully planned (research → VALIDATION.md → D-07 scope locked to full boundary → pattern map → SDK-READ-01..04 registered in REQUIREMENTS.md → 12 plans/7 waves → plan-checker PASSED → coverage gates 13/13), a follow-up todo was logged for a non-blocking gap, and execution began sequentially on the main tree. Wave 1 (68.2-01, the security-critical ROT-07 read-path gate) completed and was independently spot-checked (296/296 tests passing); Wave 2 (68.2-02) was dispatched. A separate git worktree for phase 69 was created off origin/main for parallel independent work.

repo: gsd-tools commit helper can report `commit_failed` even when the commit actually lands in git log — a known false-negative; always verify with `git log` rather than trusting the reported status.
Nyquist validation requires a `## Validation Architecture` section in RESEARCH.md to populate VALIDATION.md.
The intel API-surface extraction (§7.9) can return 0 symbols for this monorepo — it's hint-only, so omit it from planner prompts when empty rather than passing noise.
Schema-gate planner contribution should be skipped when a phase touches zero ORM/DB schema files (this phase was SDK/web codec-only).

plan:pre UI capability hook did not activate for phase 68.2 because the registry's `when` condition correctly classified it as an architecture/refactor phase, not a net-new UI surface — the lower-level ui-plan-gate check reporting `block:true` is irrelevant unless a UI hook is actually active.

Executor worktrees in this pnpm monorepo need their own `pnpm install`, making per-wave worktree churn expensive; for a phase with 5 of 7 waves single-plan, sequential execution on the main tree is more robust and equally correct when same-wave plans are file-disjoint.

worktree.baseRef config of 'head' means executor worktrees fork from live HEAD (carrying uncommitted PLAN.md files), not from origin/main — critical to verify before dispatching executors into worktrees.
git fetch failed from this sandboxed session (no network access to GitHub), but the last-known local origin/main ref was still valid/current for creating a new worktree.

code.finding: ROT-07 anti-rollback gate (enforceResolved) added at root resolve site in resolvePublishedNode
ROT-07 anti-rollback gate (enforceResolved) added at dfsFindFolder child loop
Pre-existing write-path ROT-07 gate location, used as reference for adding the new read-path gates

workflow: For research-only mode workflows, distinguish auto-use (no flag, existing RESEARCH.md), force-refresh (--research), and view-only (--view) paths to support cheap correction-without-replanning loops.

When a decision gate surfaces a scope ambiguity that changes acceptance criteria (e.g., D-07's literal wording sweeping in off-path files), pause and ask the user rather than assuming, then lock the resolution into CONTEXT.md so the planner treats it as decided.
After wave completion, independently re-run acceptance/gate tests rather than solely trusting the executor's self-reported summary, especially for security-critical foundation waves.

When user requests a worktree for parallel independent phase work, use plain `git worktree add` (not a tool that would relocate the current session) so the orchestrator can remain in the original checkout driving ongoing execution.

Use AskUserQuestion at genuine decision gates (research vs skip, scope boundary, auto-advance vs pause) rather than silently choosing a path, even under auto_advance config, when stakes are high (security-critical, multi-wave).

friction: gsd-tools query commit reported a false 'commit_failed' status multiple times despite commits landing successfully, requiring manual git log verification each time.
Post-planning gap-analysis gate output had control characters that broke the JSON parser, requiring a direct check invocation instead.
git fetch could not reach GitHub from the sandboxed session, blocking a true origin/main refresh before creating the phase-69 worktree (mitigated by using the last-known-good local ref).
Intel API-surface extraction returned 0 symbols for the monorepo, requiring the extraction step to be judged useless and skipped.
open_items: D-03's poll-invalidation leg lacks dedicated automated test coverage (only grep-level checks in Plan 09) — logged as todo 2026-07-06-d03-poll-invalidation-lacks-automated-coverage.md for follow-up gap closure.

Phase 69 planning/execution (Rust/Desktop FUSE/WinFsp) deferred to a separate worktree/session; recommended to start with /gsd-discuss-phase 69 due to an under-specified grant-root scope algorithm and an unresolved FUSE delete authority model question.

Phase 69's design-mirroring dependency on 68.2 (mirroring the SDK-owned read-chain design on the Rust side) needs manual cross-branch reference since the phase-69 worktree (off origin/main) doesn't carry 68.2's CONTEXT/RESEARCH docs.

Remaining waves 3–7 of phase 68.2 execution still pending at end of transcript (write facade + desync e2e, web rewire + store collapse, off-path pockets, delete services + grep gate, mirror revert + full web-e2e gate).
